---
title: "A tour of the editor window"
description: "Name each part of the editor window, and size its panes the way you like them."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Each project opens in one window. This page names its parts and says where to read about each one.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Window ▸ Minimize', 'Window ▸ Zoom']}
  keys="⌘M"
  tools="render_frame"
/>

<Shot
  name="04-editor.window"
  alt="The editor window with a small project open. The toolbar runs across the top, with the playhead at 00:00:02:15 of 00:00:05:07. Below it the preview shows a navy frame with the words Frame Job and a lower-third title, and the inspector on the right says Select a clip to edit its properties. At the bottom the timeline holds four tracks of clips with the playhead through them."
/>

## Window layout

| Part | Where | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Title bar](#title-bar) | Top | The project's name, its canvas size and frame rate, and "edited" |
| [Toolbar](#toolbar) | Under the title bar | Transport, timecode, preview zoom, **Safe** and **Export…** |
| [Preview](#preview) | Middle left | The frame under the playhead |
| [Inspector](/getting-started/inspector/) | Middle right | The Clip, Media, Document, Transcript and Assistant tabs |
| [Timeline bar](#timeline-bar) | Above the timeline | The selection block, clip buttons, **Snap**, the level meter, zoom and track size |
| [Timeline](/timeline/tracks/) | Bottom | The ruler, the track headers and the lanes |

A new window sizes itself to the canvas, up to 1280 × 720, plus the panes around it. It's never more than 85 % of the screen, so a 4K project doesn't open a 4K window. The smallest a window can be is 900 × 620 points.

## Title bar

The title follows the project's name and changes when you save or rename it. A blank project reads "Untitled Project". A movie you've opened but not saved reads as the movie's name.

The subtitle gives the canvas size and frame rate, then "edited" while there are unsaved changes:

`1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · edited`

"edited" clears after <kbd>⌘S</kbd> and after every silent autosave. It's the only sign of unsaved changes: projects autosave in place, so the close button shows no dot. See [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/).

The subtitle updates after any change to the canvas, including one an agent makes.

## Toolbar

From left to right:

| Control | What it does | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go to Start (<kbd>Home</kbd>) | Moves the playhead to the start | [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) |
| Previous Edit Point (<kbd>↑</kbd>) | Jumps back to the last edit point | [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) |
| Play / Pause (<kbd>Space</kbd>) | Plays and pauses | [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/) |
| Next Edit Point (<kbd>↓</kbd>) | Jumps forward to the next edit point | [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) |
| Go to End (<kbd>End</kbd>) | Moves the playhead to the end | [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) |
| Loop | Turns looping on and off | [Loop playback](/timeline/loop/) |
| Timecode | Shows the playhead's time, then `/` and the length of the timeline. Click the time to type one. | [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) |
| Preview zoom | Picks **Fit**, **50%**, **100%** or **200%** | [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/) |
| **Safe** | Shows the safe-area guides on the preview | [Safe areas](/canvas/safe-areas/) |
| **Export…** (<kbd>⌘E</kbd>) | Opens the export sheet | [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/) |

## Preview

The preview shows the frame under the playhead at canvas size, letterboxed in a grey well. A caption under it gives the size and rate, for example `960 × 540 · 30 fps`. See [The preview](/timeline/preview/) for everything it does.

## Timeline bar

The bar above the time ruler names the selection and holds the tools that act on clips. From left to right:

- **The selection block.** It says what's selected.
- **Eight clip buttons.** One click each, and each button's tooltip names its key.
- **Snap.** Turns [snapping](/timeline/snapping/) on and off.
- **The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/).** It takes the spare width in the bar, so in a narrow window it shrinks and can disappear.

---
title: "Core concepts"
description: "The ideas the rest of these docs lean on: projects, media and clips, tracks, the canvas, actions, nests and the frame grid."
---

A few ideas run through everything in Frame Job. This page says what each one is and links to where it's covered. For a quick definition of a single word, see the [Glossary](/reference/glossary/).

## Project

A project is one `.framejob` package: a single file in the Finder that holds the edit and its caches. The edit is the canvas, the media list, the tracks, the clips and the markers. Each open project has its own window.

Your footage stays where it is, and the project remembers where to find it. If you want copies inside the package, ask for them with [Consolidate Media…](/projects/consolidate-media/). See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).

## Media and clips

**Media** is a file the project knows about. A **clip** is one placement of something on the timeline. A new clip from the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) covers the whole file, and you can place the same file as many times as you like.

| Clip kind | What it plays |
| --- | --- |
| video | A movie file's picture, with its sound if it has any |
| audio | A sound with no picture |
| still | One frozen frame of a movie |
| image | A picture file, such as a PNG, JPEG or HEIC |
| text | [Words you type](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/) |
| shape | [A drawn shape](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/) |
| graphic | [A motion graphic](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/) |
| nest | [A group of clips](#nests) standing as one |
| adjustment | [A grade](/color/adjustment-clips/) applied to everything behind it. It draws nothing of its own. |

Every clip that draws (video, image, still, text, shape, graphic and nest) is placed and edited the same way, with the same gestures and the same Picture sections. Where a kind differs, its page says so.

## Tracks and stacking

There is one kind of track, and it holds any clip, so one track can mix kinds.

Tracks stack back to front. The top lane is the front-most and the bottom lane is the back, so a track higher in the timeline draws in front. See [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/).

## The canvas

The canvas is the fixed frame every clip is composited into, at the project's size and frame rate. You set its size, rate and background colour on the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/).

A clip is placed on the canvas. Moving or scaling a clip never changes the canvas. See [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/).

## Actions

An action is a span of time on one clip over which its properties ease to an end state. When the span is over, the clip holds that state until a later action changes it. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).

## Nests

A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. The group then moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing.

You can open a nest and edit inside it, and nests can contain nests, up to eight levels deep. A nest's canvas is fixed at the project's size at the moment you nest. See [Nests](/editing/nests/).

## The frame grid

Every time you set lands on a whole frame of the project's rate, so typed times, drags and agent calls all round to the grid. A clip is always at least one frame long. See [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/).

## Why clips never push each other

Dragging a clip never shoves its neighbours. A drop that the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/) won't allow springs back and moves nothing else. A clip dropped to overlap the clip before it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap.

Other clips move only when a command says so: Ripple Delete, Close Gap, Insert and, for an agent, Insert Time. Locked tracks stay put through all of them.

## Related

- [Your first edit](/getting-started/first-edit/)
- [A tour of the editor window](/getting-started/editor-window/)
- [Glossary](/reference/glossary/)

---
title: "The inspector"
description: "Find your way around the inspector's five tabs, the Clip tab's sub-tabs and its folding sections."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The inspector is the panel at the right of the editor window. It's where you read and change the numbers behind what you see: the selected clips, the project's media, the project itself, its words and the Assistant. This page covers how it's laid out. [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/) covers how its controls behave.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['View ▸ Hide Inspector', 'View ▸ Transcript', 'View ▸ Assistant']}
  keys={['⌥⌘I', '⌃⌘T', '⌃⌘A']}
  where="The editor window, middle right"
  tools="set_clip"
/>

<Shot
  name="05-clip-picture.inspector"
  alt="The inspector on the Clip tab with a video clip selected. At the top is the clip's name, speech.mov, over the line video · 00:00:05:07 · 640×360 · 30 fps. Under it are the action lane, reading no actions, and the sub-tabs Picture, Color, Sound and Clip, with Picture active. Below them the Transform section is open, showing Scale, Position, Rotation, Opacity and Blend."
/>

## The five tabs

| Tab | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| **Clip** | The selected clips. With nothing selected it reads "Select a clip to edit its properties." |
| **Media** | Every file in the project. See [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). |
| **Document** | The project as a whole. See [The Document tab](/projects/document-tab/). |
| **Transcript** | The timeline's words. **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>) goes straight there. See [The Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/). |
| **Assistant** | A conversation that edits this project. **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>) goes straight there. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/). |

## The Clip tab's pinned block

With a clip selected, three things stay pinned at the top of the Clip tab while its sections scroll underneath: the selection header, the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) and the sub-tabs.

The selection header shows:

- **A chip** coloured by the clip's kind. It's neutral when the selection mixes kinds.
- **The name.** With one clip selected this is a field. Type to give the clip its own name, which is one undo step, "Rename Clip". Empty the field to go back to what the clip shows by default. This is the only place you can clear a clip's name.
- **A line of facts.** The kind, the duration in the project's timecode, the source's pixel size and the source's own frame rate, for example `video · 00:00:05:07 · 640×360 · 30 fps`. A clip with no source shows only the facts it has.
- **A colour dot** at the end of the name line, for a clip's [colour label](/timeline/names-and-labels/). With several clips selected it shows only when they all share the label.

With several clips selected, the header reads "3 clips selected" and gives their total duration. Renaming needs a single clip.

## Sub-tabs

The strip under the action lane splits the Clip tab into **Text**, **Shape**, **Graphic**, **Picture**, **Color**, **Sound** and **Clip**. It shows only what the selection can use, and sections that don't apply are absent, not greyed out.

| Selected | Sub-tabs |
| --- | --- |
| A movie | Picture, Color, Sound, Clip |
| A picture | Picture, Color, Clip |
| A text clip | Text, Picture, Clip |
| A shape | Shape, Picture, Clip |
| A graphic | Graphic, Picture, Clip |
| An audio-only clip | Sound, Clip |
| An adjustment clip | Color, Clip |

With a mixed selection, the rules are these:

- **Text**, **Shape** and **Graphic** appear only when every selected clip is that kind.
- **Picture** appears when a selected clip draws, unless an adjustment clip is in the selection.
- **Color** appears only when every selected clip has source pixels or is an adjustment clip. That's never true of text, a shape, a graphic, a nest or an audio-only clip.
- **Sound** appears when a selected clip has sound.
- **Clip** is always there, last.

A sub-tab you pick stays active while the selection doesn't change. A new selection starts on the first tab it has, so a text clip starts on **Text** and a shape on **Shape**.

While an action is selected, a sub-tab it changes shows a mark such as `◆2` after its label, counting what the action sets there. See [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/).

## Selection follows to the Clip tab

Clicking a clip on the timeline or the canvas moves the inspector to the **Clip** tab, even if the clip was already selected. A selection that changes any other way, such as a paste, <kbd>⌘A</kbd> or an agent, moves it only from **Media** or **Document**.

Two tabs hold their ground:

- **Transcript** stays when you click a clip, and scrolls to that clip's first word.
- **Assistant** isn't pulled away when the selection changes without a click, so the Assistant's own edits don't take you off the conversation.

Clearing the selection moves no tab.

## Fold a section

Click a section's header to fold it. A folded header keeps a one-line summary of what's inside, such as `100%` for Transform or `2 filters` for Filters, so you can read a value without opening it. The fold is remembered per section, in every window and between launches.

The summary's colour tells you about the section:

| Summary colour | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| The action colour | The selected action sets something in this section |
| Body text | The section differs from its default |
| Faint | The section is at its default |

On the Clip tab, a section you've never clicked starts closed, except Transform, a text clip's Content, a shape's Shape and a graphic's Properties. Every Media and Document section starts open.

If every section on a Clip sub-tab would be shut, the first one you haven't folded yourself opens by default. A section you closed yourself stays closed.

Inside an action, a section the action sets shows `◆1` or a higher count in its header and opens by itself, without changing what's remembered. A faint ⊘ marks a section actions don't animate. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).

Folding animates, unless **Reduce Motion** is on in macOS.

## Hide or show the inspector

Choose **View ▸ Hide Inspector** (<kbd>⌥⌘I</kbd>) and the preview takes its space. The item then reads **View ▸ Show Inspector**. The inspector is shown by default, and your choice is remembered between launches.

This menu item is the only way to hide it, because dragging the divider to the edge stops at the minimum width. **View ▸ Transcript** and **View ▸ Assistant** bring it back if it's hidden.

## Related

- [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/)
- [A tour of the editor window](/getting-started/editor-window/)
- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)
- [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/)

- **A line of facts.** The kind, the duration in the project's timecode, the source's pixel size and the source's own frame rate, for example `video · 00:00:05:07 · 640×360 · 30 fps`. A clip with no source shows only the facts it has.
- **A colour dot** at the end of the name line, for a clip's [colour label](/timeline/names-and-labels/). With several clips selected it shows only when they all share the label.

With several clips selected, the header reads "3 clips selected" and gives their total duration. Renaming needs a single clip.

## Sub-tabs

The strip under the action lane splits the Clip tab into **Text**, **Shape**, **Graphic**, **Picture**, **Color**, **Sound** and **Clip**. It shows only what the selection can use, and sections that don't apply are absent, not greyed out.

| Selected | Sub-tabs |
| --- | --- |
| A movie | Picture, Color, Sound, Clip |
| A picture | Picture, Color, Clip |
| A text clip | Text, Picture, Clip |
| A shape | Shape, Picture, Clip |
| A graphic | Graphic, Picture, Clip |
| An audio-only clip | Sound, Clip |
| An adjustment clip | Color, Clip |

With a mixed selection, the rules are these:

- **Text**, **Shape** and **Graphic** appear only when every selected clip is that kind.
- **Picture** appears when a selected clip draws, unless an adjustment clip is in the selection.
- **Color** appears only when every selected clip has source pixels or is an adjustment clip. That's never true of text, a shape, a graphic, a nest or an audio-only clip.
- **Sound** appears when a selected clip has sound.
- **Clip** is always there, last.

A sub-tab you pick stays active while the selection doesn't change. A new selection starts on the first tab it has, so a text clip starts on **Text** and a shape on **Shape**.

While an action is selected, a sub-tab it changes shows a mark such as `◆2` after its label, counting what the action sets there. See [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/).

## Selection follows to the Clip tab

Clicking a clip on the timeline or the canvas moves the inspector to the **Clip** tab, even if the clip was already selected. A selection that changes any other way, such as a paste, <kbd>⌘A</kbd> or an agent, moves it only from **Media** or **Document**.

Two tabs hold their ground:

- **Transcript** stays when you click a clip, and scrolls to that clip's first word.
- **Assistant** isn't pulled away when the selection changes without a click, so the Assistant's own edits don't take you off the conversation.

Clearing the selection moves no tab.

## Fold a section

Click a section's header to fold it. A folded header keeps a one-line summary of what's inside, such as `100%` for Transform or `2 filters` for Filters, so you can read a value without opening it. The fold is remembered per section, in every window and between launches.

The summary's colour tells you about the section:

| Summary colour | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| The action colour | The selected action sets something in this section |
| Body text | The section differs from its default |
| Faint | The section is at its default |

On the Clip tab, a section you've never clicked starts closed, except Transform, a text clip's Content, a shape's Shape and a graphic's Properties. Every Media and Document section starts open.

If every section on a Clip sub-tab would be shut, the first one you haven't folded yourself opens by default. A section you closed yourself stays closed.

Inside an action, a section the action sets shows `◆1` or a higher count in its header and opens by itself, without changing what's remembered. A faint ⊘ marks a section actions don't animate. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).

Folding animates, unless **Reduce Motion** is on in macOS.

## Hide or show the inspector

Choose **View ▸ Hide Inspector** (<kbd>⌥⌘I</kbd>) and the preview takes its space. The item then reads **View ▸ Show Inspector**. The inspector is shown by default, and your choice is remembered between launches.

This menu item is the only way to hide it, because dragging the divider to the edge stops at the minimum width. **View ▸ Transcript** and **View ▸ Assistant** bring it back if it's hidden.

## Related

- [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/)
- [A tour of the editor window](/getting-started/editor-window/)
- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)
- [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/)

---
title: "Requirements and install"
description: "What your Mac needs to run Frame Job, where to download it, and what happens the first time you open it."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Frame Job runs on an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 26 or later. There's no account to make, and you can start cutting as soon as it's in your Applications folder.

<AtAGlance
  needs={['An Apple Silicon Mac', 'macOS 26 or later']}
/>

## What Frame Job needs

| You need | Details |
| --- | --- |
| An Apple Silicon Mac | Frame Job is built for Apple Silicon alone, so an Intel Mac can't run it. |
| macOS 26 or later | 26.0 is the oldest system it opens on. |
| An account | None. There's nothing to sign up for. |
| An API key | None to edit. Only the Assistant and cloud transcription need one, and each runs on [your own key](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/). Everything else works without a key. |

:::note
M1 and M2 Macs have no AV1 decoder. They can export [AV1](/export/av1-and-vp9/), but they can't play the file or import it again. The rest of the editor isn't affected.
:::

## Download and install

<Steps>

1. Download the newest build: [FrameJob.dmg](https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/releases/latest/download/FrameJob.dmg). This link always gives you the latest release.

2. Open the DMG.

3. Drag Frame Job to Applications.

</Steps>

The download is signed and notarized, and it [updates itself](/getting-started/updates/).

A copy you build yourself has no updater. To build one, see [Developing Frame Job](https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/blob/main/docs/developing.md).

## First launch

Frame Job asks you for nothing the first time it opens: no account, no key and no system permission. As with any app downloaded from the internet, macOS may ask you to confirm that you want to open it.

With nothing to open, it shows the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/), with **Open Video…**, **New Project**, **New Recording…** and your recent projects.

<Shot
  name="01-welcome.window"
  alt="The Welcome window: the Frame Job mark and name, the line Open a file. Start cutting., the buttons Open Video…, New Project and New Recording…, and a line of the file types it opens."
/>

Three things come later, and only when you get to them:

- **System permissions.** macOS asks for Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera or Input Monitoring only when you press **Record** in the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), and only for what that recording uses. Frame Job never asks at launch. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
- **Automatic updates.** The second time you open the downloaded copy, it asks whether to check for updates automatically.
- **API keys.** They're optional, and you set them in **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>), which works with no project open.

## Related

- [Your first edit](/getting-started/first-edit/)
- [Updates](/getting-started/updates/)
- [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/)

---
title: "Your first edit"
description: "One short walk from start to finish: open a movie, cut a section out, add a title and export an H.264 file."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

This walk takes one movie from your Mac to a finished file. You'll open it, cut a section out, add a title and export an H.264 movie. Each step links to the page that covers it in full.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Open…', 'Edit ▸ Ripple Delete', 'File ▸ Save', 'File ▸ Export…']}
  keys={['⌘O', 'Space', 'I', 'O', '⌘⌫', 'T', '⌘S', '⌘E']}
/>

## Open a movie

Choose **File ▸ Open…** (<kbd>⌘O</kbd>) and pick a `.mov` or `.mp4`. **Open Video…** in the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/) and a drop on the Dock icon do the same.

You get an untitled project sized and rated to the file, with the movie as the first clip on Track 1, starting at 0. See [Start a project](/projects/start-a-project/) for the other ways in.

## Find the section

Press <kbd>Space</kbd> to play and again to pause. Click the [ruler](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/) to move the playhead straight to a moment.

## Cut it out

1. Move the playhead to the start of the section and press <kbd>I</kbd>.
2. Move it to the end of the section and press <kbd>O</kbd>. The [range](/timeline/in-out-range/) is now shaded across the ruler and the lanes.
3. Check that the left end of the timeline bar reads **No selection**. If it doesn't, click an empty part of a lane.
4. Choose **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** (<kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>).

Frame Job cuts every unlocked clip at both ends of the range, removes what lies between and closes the gap. The range stays set after the cut, so press <kbd>⌥X</kbd> to clear it.

:::caution
With a clip selected, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> removes the whole clip, not the range. That's why step 3 matters.
:::

See [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/) for how the delete commands differ.

## Add a title

Move the playhead to where the title should start and press <kbd>T</kbd>.

The title goes on the front-most track if there's room at the playhead, and on a new front track if there isn't. With your movie under the playhead, that means a new track. It reads "Title" in Source Sans 3 Bold at 72 px, white and centred, and it lasts 5 seconds.

The new clip is selected, so the **Text** sub-tab opens on it. Type your words in **Content** and press <kbd>Return</kbd>. See [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/) for the rest.

## Save the project

Choose **File ▸ Save** (<kbd>⌘S</kbd>). Frame Job writes a `.framejob` package, and offers to put it next to the source file. After that, the project autosaves. See [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/).

## Export the movie

1. Choose **File ▸ Export…** (<kbd>⌘E</kbd>), or the **Export…** button at the right of the toolbar. The command is greyed out while the timeline is empty.
2. With nothing remembered from an earlier export, the sheet opens on **H.264 (MP4)** at the project's own size. Leave it there.
3. Choose **Export…**, then pick a name and a place in the save panel.

Frame Job writes the file behind a progress sheet. When it finishes, **Show in Finder** takes you to the file. See [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/) for every other format and setting.

## If you make a mistake

Press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> at any step to take back one edit.

## Related

- [A tour of the editor window](/getting-started/editor-window/)
- [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/)
- [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/)

---
title: "A tour of the editor window"
description: "Name each part of the editor window, and size its panes the way you like them."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Each project opens in one window. This page names its parts and says where to read about each one.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Window ▸ Minimize', 'Window ▸ Zoom']}
  keys="⌘M"
  tools="render_frame"
/>

<Shot
  name="04-editor.window"
  alt="The editor window with a small project open. The toolbar runs across the top, with the playhead at 00:00:02:15 of 00:00:05:07. Below it the preview shows a navy frame with the words Frame Job and a lower-third title, and the inspector on the right says Select a clip to edit its properties. At the bottom the timeline holds four tracks of clips with the playhead through them."
/>

## Window layout

| Part | Where | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Title bar](#title-bar) | Top | The project's name, its canvas size and frame rate, and "edited" |
| [Toolbar](#toolbar) | Under the title bar | Transport, timecode, preview zoom, **Safe** and **Export…** |
| [Preview](#preview) | Middle left | The frame under the playhead |
| [Inspector](/getting-started/inspector/) | Middle right | The Clip, Media, Document, Transcript and Assistant tabs |
| [Timeline bar](#timeline-bar) | Above the timeline | The selection block, clip buttons, **Snap**, the level meter, zoom and track size |
| [Timeline](/timeline/tracks/) | Bottom | The ruler, the track headers and the lanes |

A new window sizes itself to the canvas, up to 1280 × 720, plus the panes around it. It's never more than 85 % of the screen, so a 4K project doesn't open a 4K window. The smallest a window can be is 900 × 620 points.

## Title bar

The title follows the project's name and changes when you save or rename it. A blank project reads "Untitled Project". A movie you've opened but not saved reads as the movie's name.

The subtitle gives the canvas size and frame rate, then "edited" while there are unsaved changes:

`1920 × 1080 · 30 fps · edited`

"edited" clears after <kbd>⌘S</kbd> and after every silent autosave. It's the only sign of unsaved changes: projects autosave in place, so the close button shows no dot. See [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/).

The subtitle updates after any change to the canvas, including one an agent makes.

## Toolbar

From left to right:

| Control | What it does | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go to Start (<kbd>Home</kbd>) | Moves the playhead to the start | [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) |
| Previous Edit Point (<kbd>↑</kbd>) | Jumps back to the last edit point | [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) |
| Play / Pause (<kbd>Space</kbd>) | Plays and pauses | [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/) |
| Next Edit Point (<kbd>↓</kbd>) | Jumps forward to the next edit point | [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) |
| Go to End (<kbd>End</kbd>) | Moves the playhead to the end | [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) |
| Loop | Turns looping on and off | [Loop playback](/timeline/loop/) |
| Timecode | Shows the playhead's time, then `/` and the length of the timeline. Click the time to type one. | [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/) |
| Preview zoom | Picks **Fit**, **50%**, **100%** or **200%** | [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/) |
| **Safe** | Shows the safe-area guides on the preview | [Safe areas](/canvas/safe-areas/) |
| **Export…** (<kbd>⌘E</kbd>) | Opens the export sheet | [The export sheet](/export/export-sheet/) |

## Preview

The preview shows the frame under the playhead at canvas size, letterboxed in a grey well. A caption under it gives the size and rate, for example `960 × 540 · 30 fps`. See [The preview](/timeline/preview/) for everything it does.

## Timeline bar

The bar above the time ruler names the selection and holds the tools that act on clips. From left to right:

- **The selection block.** It says what's selected.
- **Eight clip buttons.** One click each, and each button's tooltip names its key.
- **Snap.** Turns [snapping](/timeline/snapping/) on and off.
- **The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/).** It takes the spare width in the bar, so in a narrow window it shrinks and can disappear.
- **The zoom controls.** −, a slider, + and Fit (<kbd>⇧Z</kbd>). See [Zoom and scroll the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/).
- **S, M and L.** Sets the [track height](/timeline/track-height/).

### The selection block

| Selected | The block shows |
| --- | --- |
| One clip | A chip in the clip's kind colour, the clip's name, and its track and kind under that, for example `Track 2 · video` |
| Several clips | A count such as `3 clips`, over the track or `2 tracks`, and the kind or `mixed` |
| Nothing | No selection |

The block has a fixed width, so a long name is cut short and the tools beside it never move.

### The clip buttons

| Button | Key | Read more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Split | <kbd>⌘T</kbd> | [Split clips](/editing/splitting/) |
| Trim Start to Playhead | <kbd>W</kbd> | [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/) |
| Trim End to Playhead | <kbd>E</kbd> | [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/) |
| Ripple Delete | <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> | [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/) |
| Add Marker | <kbd>M</kbd> | [Markers](/timeline/markers/) |
| Duplicate | <kbd>⌘D</kbd> | [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/) |
| Add Text | <kbd>T</kbd> | [Text clips](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/) |
| Add Shape | None | [Shape clips](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/) |

## Pane dividers

Drag the divider left of the inspector to set its width, and the divider above the timeline to set its height. New windows open at the sizes you chose, and the sizes are remembered between launches.

| Pane | Range | To start |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inspector width | 280 to 440 points | 304 points |
| Timeline height | 140 points up to 60 % of the window | 300 points |

The canvas keeps at least 380 points of width, and the area above the timeline at least 220 points of height.

Only dragging a divider saves a size. Resizing the window, restoring a window, or hiding and showing the inspector changes nothing that's remembered, and the inspector's width isn't saved while it's hidden.

Dragging the inspector's divider to the edge stops at the minimum width. To hide the inspector, see [The inspector](/getting-started/inspector/).

## Minimize and Zoom

These are the standard window commands. **Window ▸ Minimize** (<kbd>⌘M</kbd>) sends the window to the Dock, and **Window ▸ Zoom** makes it larger or smaller.

**Window ▸ Zoom** sizes the window. **View ▸ Zoom In** and **View ▸ Zoom Out** zoom the [preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/).

## Related

- [The inspector](/getting-started/inspector/)
- [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/)
- [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/)

---
title: "Core concepts"
description: "The ideas the rest of these docs lean on: projects, media and clips, tracks, the canvas, actions, nests and the frame grid."
---

A few ideas run through everything in Frame Job. This page says what each one is and links to where it's covered. For a quick definition of a single word, see the [Glossary](/reference/glossary/).

## Project

A project is one `.framejob` package: a single file in the Finder that holds the edit and its caches. The edit is the canvas, the media list, the tracks, the clips and the markers. Each open project has its own window.

Your footage stays where it is, and the project remembers where to find it. If you want copies inside the package, ask for them with [Consolidate Media…](/projects/consolidate-media/). See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).

## Media and clips

**Media** is a file the project knows about. A **clip** is one placement of something on the timeline. A new clip from the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) covers the whole file, and you can place the same file as many times as you like.

| Clip kind | What it plays |
| --- | --- |
| video | A movie file's picture, with its sound if it has any |
| audio | A sound with no picture |
| still | One frozen frame of a movie |
| image | A picture file, such as a PNG, JPEG or HEIC |
| text | [Words you type](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/) |
| shape | [A drawn shape](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/) |
| graphic | [A motion graphic](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/) |
| nest | [A group of clips](#nests) standing as one |
| adjustment | [A grade](/color/adjustment-clips/) applied to everything behind it. It draws nothing of its own. |

Every clip that draws (video, image, still, text, shape, graphic and nest) is placed and edited the same way, with the same gestures and the same Picture sections. Where a kind differs, its page says so.

## Tracks and stacking

There is one kind of track, and it holds any clip, so one track can mix kinds.

Tracks stack back to front. The top lane is the front-most and the bottom lane is the back, so a track higher in the timeline draws in front. See [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/).

## The canvas

The canvas is the fixed frame every clip is composited into, at the project's size and frame rate. You set its size, rate and background colour on the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/).

A clip is placed on the canvas. Moving or scaling a clip never changes the canvas. See [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/).

## Actions

An action is a span of time on one clip over which its properties ease to an end state. When the span is over, the clip holds that state until a later action changes it. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).

## Nests

A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. The group then moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing.

You can open a nest and edit inside it, and nests can contain nests, up to eight levels deep. A nest's canvas is fixed at the project's size at the moment you nest. See [Nests](/editing/nests/).

## The frame grid

Every time you set lands on a whole frame of the project's rate, so typed times, drags and agent calls all round to the grid. A clip is always at least one frame long. See [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/).

## Why clips never push each other

Dragging a clip never shoves its neighbours. A drop that the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/) won't allow springs back and moves nothing else. A clip dropped to overlap the clip before it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap.

Other clips move only when a command says so: Ripple Delete, Close Gap, Insert and, for an agent, Insert Time. Locked tracks stay put through all of them.

## Related

- [Your first edit](/getting-started/first-edit/)
- [A tour of the editor window](/getting-started/editor-window/)
- [Glossary](/reference/glossary/)

---
title: "The inspector"
description: "Find your way around the inspector's five tabs, the Clip tab's sub-tabs and its folding sections."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The inspector is the panel at the right of the editor window. It's where you read and change the numbers behind what you see: the selected clips, the project's media, the project itself, its words and the Assistant. This page covers how it's laid out. [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/) covers how its controls behave.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['View ▸ Hide Inspector', 'View ▸ Transcript', 'View ▸ Assistant']}
  keys={['⌥⌘I', '⌃⌘T', '⌃⌘A']}
  where="The editor window, middle right"
  tools="set_clip"
/>

<Shot
  name="05-clip-picture.inspector"
  alt="The inspector on the Clip tab with a video clip selected. At the top is the clip's name, speech.mov, over the line video · 00:00:05:07 · 640×360 · 30 fps. Under it are the action lane, reading no actions, and the sub-tabs Picture, Color, Sound and Clip, with Picture active. Below them the Transform section is open, showing Scale, Position, Rotation, Opacity and Blend."
/>

## The five tabs

| Tab | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| **Clip** | The selected clips. With nothing selected it reads "Select a clip to edit its properties." |
| **Media** | Every file in the project. See [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). |
| **Document** | The project as a whole. See [The Document tab](/projects/document-tab/). |
| **Transcript** | The timeline's words. **View ▸ Transcript** (<kbd>⌃⌘T</kbd>) goes straight there. See [The Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/). |
| **Assistant** | A conversation that edits this project. **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>) goes straight there. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/). |

## The Clip tab's pinned block

With a clip selected, three things stay pinned at the top of the Clip tab while its sections scroll underneath: the selection header, the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) and the sub-tabs.

The selection header shows:

- **A chip** coloured by the clip's kind. It's neutral when the selection mixes kinds.
- **The name.** With one clip selected this is a field. Type to give the clip its own name, which is one undo step, "Rename Clip". Empty the field to go back to what the clip shows by default. This is the only place you can clear a clip's name.
- **A line of facts.** The kind, the duration in the project's timecode, the source's pixel size and the source's own frame rate, for example `video · 00:00:05:07 · 640×360 · 30 fps`. A clip with no source shows only the facts it has.
- **A colour dot** at the end of the name line, for a clip's [colour label](/timeline/names-and-labels/). With several clips selected it shows only when they all share the label.

With several clips selected, the header reads "3 clips selected" and gives their total duration. Renaming needs a single clip.

## Sub-tabs

The strip under the action lane splits the Clip tab into **Text**, **Shape**, **Graphic**, **Picture**, **Color**, **Sound** and **Clip**. It shows only what the selection can use, and sections that don't apply are absent, not greyed out.

| Selected | Sub-tabs |
| --- | --- |
| A movie | Picture, Color, Sound, Clip |
| A picture | Picture, Color, Clip |
| A text clip | Text, Picture, Clip |
| A shape | Shape, Picture, Clip |
| A graphic | Graphic, Picture, Clip |
| An audio-only clip | Sound, Clip |
| An adjustment clip | Color, Clip |

With a mixed selection, the rules are these:

- **Text**, **Shape** and **Graphic** appear only when every selected clip is that kind.
- **Picture** appears when a selected clip draws, unless an adjustment clip is in the selection.
- **Color** appears only when every selected clip has source pixels or is an adjustment clip. That's never true of text, a shape, a graphic, a nest or an audio-only clip.
- **Sound** appears when a selected clip has sound.
- **Clip** is always there, last.

A sub-tab you pick stays active while the selection doesn't change. A new selection starts on the first tab it has, so a text clip starts on **Text** and a shape on **Shape**.

While an action is selected, a sub-tab it changes shows a mark such as `◆2` after its label, counting what the action sets there. See [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/).

## Selection follows to the Clip tab

Clicking a clip on the timeline or the canvas moves the inspector to the **Clip** tab, even if the clip was already selected. A selection that changes any other way, such as a paste, <kbd>⌘A</kbd> or an agent, moves it only from **Media** or **Document**.

Two tabs hold their ground:

- **Transcript** stays when you click a clip, and scrolls to that clip's first word.
- **Assistant** isn't pulled away when the selection changes without a click, so the Assistant's own edits don't take you off the conversation.

Clearing the selection moves no tab.

## Fold a section

Click a section's header to fold it. A folded header keeps a one-line summary of what's inside, such as `100%` for Transform or `2 filters` for Filters, so you can read a value without opening it. The fold is remembered per section, in every window and between launches.

The summary's colour tells you about the section:

| Summary colour | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| The action colour | The selected action sets something in this section |
| Body text | The section differs from its default |
| Faint | The section is at its default |

On the Clip tab, a section you've never clicked starts closed, except Transform, a text clip's Content, a shape's Shape and a graphic's Properties. Every Media and Document section starts open.

If every section on a Clip sub-tab would be shut, the first one you haven't folded yourself opens by default. A section you closed yourself stays closed.

Inside an action, a section the action sets shows `◆1` or a higher count in its header and opens by itself, without changing what's remembered. A faint ⊘ marks a section actions don't animate. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).

Folding animates, unless **Reduce Motion** is on in macOS.

## Hide or show the inspector

Choose **View ▸ Hide Inspector** (<kbd>⌥⌘I</kbd>) and the preview takes its space. The item then reads **View ▸ Show Inspector**. The inspector is shown by default, and your choice is remembered between launches.

This menu item is the only way to hide it, because dragging the divider to the edge stops at the minimum width. **View ▸ Transcript** and **View ▸ Assistant** bring it back if it's hidden.
